message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Masterful atmosphere, iconic performances, psychological terror. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | Suspenseful paranoia, groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Wes Craven | Introduces Freddy Krueger, blends dream logic with slasher thrills. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | Jonathan Demme | Psychological thriller with chilling characters (Hannibal Lecter). |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez | Found‑footage style that created a new sub‑genre. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑moving zombie outbreak, social commentary. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Dark, twisted moral dilemmas, cult‑classic slasher. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage that made a huge impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Supernatural horror with strong storytelling. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | Meta‑take on horror tropes, clever twists. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | Unique premise, creepy atmosphere. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | Period horror with unsettling dread. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | Social satire meets horror, sharp commentary. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | Silence‑based tension, emotional stakes. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | Daylight horror, unsettling folk rituals. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Modern retelling, psychological terror. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** | Nia DaCosta | Reimagining a classic legend, social relevance. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** | Scott Derrickson | Supernatural thriller with a unique premise. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | Gerard Johnstone | AI horror with a creepy twist. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
